# Psalm 87 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** A psalm of the descendants of Korah. A song. His city stands on the holy mountains.

**2** The LORD loves the gates of Zion more than any other place in Israel.

**3** What amazing things are said about you, city of God! Selah

**4** God declares: 'When I list the nations who acknowledge me — Egypt, Babylon, Philistia, Tyre, even distant Ethiopia — each one will be noted: "This person was born in Zion."'

**5** And of Zion it will be said, 'People from every nation were born here!' The Most High himself will make her strong.

**6** When the LORD registers the nations, he will write next to each name: 'This one belongs to Zion.' Selah

**7** Then the singers and dancers will say together: 'Everything I am flows from you!'

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **87:4-6**: This tiny psalm is one of the most radical in the Bible. God is claiming that people from Israel's worst enemies — Egypt, Babylon, Philistia — are 'born in Zion.' It's a vision of universal belonging that shatters every nationalistic boundary.

- **87:7**: The final verse is pure celebration: 'Everything I am flows from you.' When you belong to God's city, you discover the source of everything good.

— PNEUMA
